context: Tests whether the agent applies the shell-script-reviewer skill's error-handling stance to a script wearing the 'unofficial strict mode' header: flagging the presence of set -e/set -u as an anti-pattern (Style, at most Medium) while explicitly keeping -o pipefail, refusing to recommend adding strict mode, and STILL reporting unchecked critical commands (a cd inside a function called from an && guard chain) as Correctness findings because -e cannot be trusted — plus refusing the classic wrong one-line fix of double-quoting $(ls ...) output.

checklist.name: set -e / set -u flagged for removal
checklist.description: The review flags the presence of `set -e` (and `-u`) in the strict-mode header as a finding and recommends REMOVING them while keeping what is safe — it does not merely note the header as good practice or leave it unmentioned.

checklist.name: Anti-pattern finding correctly classified
checklist.description: The -e/-u finding is Category Style and severity no higher than Medium (Low or Medium), per the skill's stance that it is a maintainability finding, not a safety one — it is neither silenced as best practice nor inflated to High/Critical.

checklist.name: Never recommends adding strict mode
checklist.description: Nowhere in the report does the agent recommend adding `set -e`, `set -u`, or `set -euo pipefail` (or expanding strict mode), and the report does not list the absence of a strict-mode header anywhere as a gap; critiques of the script come from the documented explicit-checks stance instead.

checklist.name: pipefail and IFS narrowing explicitly kept
checklist.description: The recommended replacement for the header keeps `set -o pipefail` (and may keep the IFS narrowing / call them unambiguously safe defense-in-depth) instead of discarding the whole header wholesale.

checklist.name: Unchecked cd reported regardless of set -e
checklist.description: The review reports the unchecked `cd "$SNAPSHOT_ROOT"` in snapshot() as a Correctness finding with an explicit `cd ... || exit` (or `|| return`) check, even though `set -e` is present — and explicitly does not treat -e as validating it; the fix is explicit per-command checks.

checklist.name: Guard-chain failure swallowing explained
checklist.description: The review recognises that `snapshot && prune_old "$1"` inside main() suppresses errexit for the whole chain (including any critical command inside the functions it calls, since failures land on commands that are part of an &&/|| list) so a failed snapshot silently continues to list and print 'snapshot complete' — and proposes explicit checks rather than leaning on -e.

checklist.name: ls-loop fixed per authority, not by quoting
checklist.description: The `for f in $(ls "$SNAPSHOT_ROOT")` finding is marked True Correctness (one of the few defects ShellCheck catches) but the review does NOT propose the tempting one-line fix of double-quoting the $(ls ...) substitution; with static-analysis coverage confirmed the proposed fix is a glob or `find ... -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d ''`, citing SC2045 / BashPitfalls.

checklist.name: Report follows the output skeleton
checklist.description: review-report.md states the dialect (bash) and uses the skill's skeleton: findings grouped by severity with locations as file:line (Severity and Category named per finding), concrete Current/Fix snippets, and a summary count table by severity and by category.

checklist.name: No invented severity and no false safety claims
checklist.description: The review neither invents Critical-severity findings the fixture does not support (no untrusted-input eval, no temp-file race here) nor asserts the script is safe because the strict header is present; findings drive the graded output paths, not the header.
